3. MINIMUM PRESCRIBED ATTENDANCE THRESHOLD

3.1 Mandatory Standard: Every enrolled student must maintain a minimum cumulative attendance of 75.0% in every registered lecture (theory), tutorial, and laboratory course component across the fifteen-week semester.
3.2 Computation Principle: Attendance percentages are computed individually per course code as the ratio of total instructional sessions attended to total sessions conducted, as aggregated by the AttendEdge platform.
3.3 Continuous Monitoring: Attendance registers are updated continuously. Students falling below 80.0% receive automated advisory notifications via UniCampus ERP and institutional email.

title: Mandatory Attendance and Condonation Policy
text:
4. CONDONATION OF ATTENDANCE SHORTAGE (65.0% TO 74.9%)

4.1 Eligible Condonation Band: The Academic Council authorizes the Dean of Academic Affairs to exercise discretionary condonation solely for students whose cumulative attendance in a course falls strictly between 65.0% and 74.9%.
4.2 Statutory Grounds for Condonation:
  a) Authenticated Medical Grounds: Acute illness, surgical intervention, contagious disease quarantine, or severe trauma requiring documented hospitalization verified by the Campus Health Centre.
  b) Sanctioned Institutional On-Duty (OD) Representation: Excused absence granted by the Department of Student Affairs for officially representing Demo University in approved inter-university athletic tournaments, national technical symposiums, or accredited competitive hackathons.
4.3 Strict Limitation: Condonation is not a matter of right. Applications must be formally substantiated with verified institutional documentation uploaded to ResolveDesk at least five working days prior to the commencement of Semester End Examinations (SEE).

title: Mandatory Attendance and Condonation Policy
text:
5. ACADEMIC DETENTION (ATTENDANCE STRICTLY BELOW 65.0%)

5.1 Absolute Prohibition: Students whose attendance in any registered course falls strictly below 65.0% at the close of instructional teaching are summarily detained from appearing in the Semester End Examination for that course.
5.2 Non-Waivable Status: Neither departmental Heads of Department nor executive university leadership possess statutory authority to condone attendance below 65.0% under any circumstance, medical or otherwise.
5.3 Academic Consequence: The student is awarded a 'W' (Withheld / Detention) grade or 'SA' (Shortage of Attendance) grade on the formal grade report. The student forfeits all Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) marks accrued for the semester.
5.4 Remediation Pathway: Detained students must re-register for the complete course during a subsequent regular academic semester or during the intensive seven-week fast-track summer term, fulfilling full instructional attendance and internal assessment requirements.

title: Course Add/Drop and Course Withdrawal Policy

3. THE OFFICIAL ADD/DROP WINDOW

3.1 Operational Timeline: The formal Course Add/Drop window commences on Day 1 of instructional classes and terminates strictly at 5:00 PM on the tenth (10th) working day of the active academic semester.
3.2 Permissible Modifications: Within this statutory ten-day window, students may:
  a) Add elective courses, provided section enrollment quotas have not reached physical room capacities.
  b) Drop previously registered elective courses without academic penalty.
  c) Request class section re-allocations to resolve demonstrated timetable clashes.
3.3 Credit Boundary Compliance: Any modification executed during the Add/Drop window must maintain the student's cumulative registration within the prescribed limits (minimum 20 credits, maximum 24 credits, or approved 28-credit overload).
3.4 Grade Log Expunction: Courses dropped prior to the expiration of the tenth working day are completely expunged from the student's academic record, leaving zero transcript notation.

2. ACADEMIC MINIMA FOR DEGREE CONFERMENT

  a) B.Tech: Successful completion of exactly 160 prescribed academic credits as structured in the program curriculum.
  b) MBA: Successful completion of 84 prescribed academic credits.

  b) For all Postgraduate degrees: A minimum terminal CGPA of 6.00 on a 10.00-point scale.
2.3 Total Backlog Liquidation: Every registered course must be cleared with a passing letter grade (O, A+, A, B+, B, C, or P). Zero 'F' (Fail) or 'I' (Incomplete) grades can remain on the permanent record.

2.2 Total Program Requirements: 160 credits distributed across Basic Sciences, Engineering Sciences, Humanities and Management, Program Core, Program Electives, Open Electives, and Capstone Projects.

text:
5. GRADING SCALE AND STATISTICAL COMPUTATIONS

5.1 10-Point Relative Grading System: Grades are awarded on a 10-point scale: O (Outstanding, 10), A+ (Excellent, 9), A (Very Good, 8), B+ (Good, 7), B (Above Average, 6), C (Average, 5), P (Pass, 4), and F (Fail, 0).
5.2 Relative Curve Mapping: Letter grades are determined using statistical normal curve distributions based on class mean and standard deviation.
5.3 SGPA and CGPA Formulas: SGPA is the weighted sum of credit-grade products divided by total credits registered in the semester. CGPA is the cumulative weighted sum across all completed terms.

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs
text:
1. STATUTORY JURISDICTION

Promulgated by the Academic Council, this regulatory code governs all master's degree programs offered at Demo University, including Master of Technology (M.Tech in Software Engineering, 72 credits) and Master of Business Administration (MBA, 84 credits).

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs
text:
2. ACADEMIC STANDING AND PROGRESSION

2.1 Grading and Cutoffs: Postgraduate programs enforce higher scholastic thresholds than undergraduate tracks. The minimum passing grade in any course is 'C' (Grade Point 5). The minimum cumulative CGPA required for degree conferment is 6.00.
2.2 Passing Standards: A student must secure a minimum of 50% aggregate (CIE + SEE) with at least 40% in the formal Semester End Examination theory paper.

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs
text:
3. MASTER'S THESIS AND DISSERTATION REGULATIONS

3.1 M.Tech Thesis: Every M.Tech candidate completes a 16-credit Dissertation across Semesters 3 and 4 (Course Code: CSE580). The thesis must produce an original technical contribution.
3.2 Plagiarism Screening: Prior to defense submission, theses undergo mandatory similarity screening via Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub in the Valmiki Central Library; similarity indices exceeding 15% are rejected.
3.3 External Defense: The dissertation is evaluated through a public defense and oral viva voce conducted by an external examiner appointed by the Controller of Examinations.

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs
text:
4. MANDATORY TEACHING ASSISTANTSHIP (TA)

All regular postgraduate scholars receiving institutional stipends must serve as Graduate Teaching Assistants for 8 to 10 hours per week in undergraduate laboratories and tutorials (ACAD-POL-007).

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs

title: Academic Regulations for Postgraduate Programs

All postgraduate program requirements must be cleared within a maximum ceiling of four (4) consecutive academic years (N + 2) from matriculation.

4. CO-TO-PO MAPPING MATRIX AND ARTICULATION LEVELS

Course Instructors, in coordination with the Course Coordinator and Program Coordinator, establish a correlation matrix linking each Course Outcome to relevant Program Outcomes using standard articulation weights:

title: Campus Recruitment Policy, CDC Registration, and One-Offer Norms
text:
2. ACADEMIC AND TRAINING ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA (POL-PLACEMENT-ELIG)

To register on the CareerHub portal and participate in campus recruitment drives, students must fulfill all statutory eligibility benchmarks:
2.1 Cumulative Academic Performance: The student must maintain a minimum aggregate of sixty percent (60%) or a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 6.50 across all completed semesters.
2.2 Backlog Arrears Prohibition: The student must have zero active backlog arrears (no uncleared 'F' or 'I' grades in theory or laboratory coursework at the time of drive registration).
2.3 Mandatory CPTD Training Attendance: Students must achieve a minimum attendance of eighty-five percent (85%) in pre-placement training modules, soft-skill bootcamps, and mock interview assessments administered by the Centre for Professional Training and Development (CPTD).
2.4 Disciplinary Standing: Students with active disciplinary suspensions or sanctions recorded by the Proctorial Board are strictly disqualified from placement participation.

title: Campus Recruitment Policy, CDC Registration, and One-Offer Norms
text:
3. ONE-STUDENT-ONE-JOB REGULATION AND CTC TIERS

To ensure equitable access to employment opportunities across the student body, Demo University enforces a strict 'One-Student-One-Job' policy governed by defined compensation tiers:
3.1 Regular Tier (Core / Mass Recruitment): Encompasses employment offers with Cost to Company (CTC) up to Rs. 8.00 Lakhs Per Annum (LPA). Once a student receives a verified offer in this category, their profile is automatically locked from subsequent Regular Tier recruitment drives.
3.2 Dream Tier Exception: A student holding a single Regular Tier offer remains eligible to participate in 'Dream Company' recruitment drives, defined strictly as corporate opportunities offering a CTC exceeding Rs. 12.00 Lakhs Per Annum (> Rs. 12 LPA).
3.3 Offer Freeze: Upon securing a Dream Tier offer, the student's placement status is frozen, and they are ineligible for any further campus recruitment drives.

section: 2. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS AND OFFICIAL POLICIES
text:
2. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS AND OFFICIAL POLICIES

Q1: What are the minimum academic eligibility requirements to register on CareerHub?
A1: Students must possess a minimum cumulative aggregate of 60% (or CGPA >= 6.50) across completed semesters, zero active backlogs, and >= 85% attendance in CPTD pre-placement training modules (POL-PLACEMENT-ELIG).

Q2: What is the 'One-Student-One-Job' rule, and how does the Dream Tier exception work?
A2: Under PLC-POL-001, once a student receives an employment offer with CTC <= Rs. 8.00 LPA (Regular Tier), they are barred from competing in further Regular Tier drives. However, they remain eligible to participate in 'Dream Company' recruitment drives offering a CTC strictly greater than Rs. 12.00 LPA (> Rs. 12 LPA). Upon securing a Dream Tier offer, the candidate cannot participate in any subsequent campus recruitment drives.

Q3: Can a student with uncleared backlogs register for campus placement drives?
A3: No. Students with active 'F' grade backlog arrears are strictly disqualified from placement drive registrations. Upon clearing backlogs via supplementary exams or summer fast-track terms, student profiles are re-evaluated for subsequent drives.

Q4: What are the penalties for missing a scheduled test or interview after registering for a company drive?
A4: Unexcused absence from any stage of an applied recruitment drive results in automatic debarment from the next three (3) consecutive placement drives for which the student is otherwise eligible.

Q5: Can placed students join their corporate employer early in the 8th semester?
A5: Yes. Under REL-012 and ACAD-POL-008, final-year students with verified corporate joining dates in February may convert their on-campus coursework into an Industry Capstone Project, subject to HOD endorsement and Dean of Academic Affairs sanction.

Q6: Where can students resolve discrepancies regarding their CareerHub profile or CGPA display?
A6: Students must log a support ticket on ResolveDesk under 'Career Services > Profile Sync'. Discrepancies are reconciled with the UniCampus ERP academic ledger within twelve (12) hours.

title: CSE201: Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) Course Syllabus and Lab Guide
text:
3. MODULAR THEORY SYLLABUS

3.1 Module 1: Complexity Analysis and Elementary Data Structures
  - Mathematical foundations of algorithmic complexity: Asymptotic notation (Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta) and recurrence relations.
  - Contiguous versus linked allocation: Dynamic memory allocation, pointer manipulation, and memory leak mitigation.
  - Linear data representations: Singly linked lists, doubly linked lists, circular buffers, and memory caching implications.
3.2 Module 2: Abstract Data Types: Stacks and Queues
  - Stack operations, array and linked implementations, recursion call-stack simulation, expression parsing (infix-to-postfix translation), and balanced delimiter matching.
  - Queue architectures: Linear queues, circular queues, double-ended queues (deque), and priority queues implemented via binary heaps.
3.3 Module 3: Non-Linear Hierarchical Representations: Trees
  - Tree terminology, binary trees, properties, array representation, and recursive/iterative traversals.
  - Binary Search Trees (BST): Insertion, search, deletion, and worst-case degeneracy.
  - Self-balancing search trees: AVL tree rotations and balance factor maintenance; introduction to Red-Black trees and B-trees for external file indexing.
3.4 Module 4: Graph Theory and Network Traversal
  - Graph representations: Adjacency matrix, adjacency lists, and compressed sparse structures.
  - Fundamental graph traversals: Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS) with cycle detection.
  - Minimum Spanning Trees (Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms) and single-source shortest paths (Dijkstra's and Bellman-Ford algorithms).
3.5 Module 5: Sorting, Searching, and Hash Tables
  - Comparative sorting paradigms: Quicksort (partitioning strategies), Mergesort, and Heapsort.
  - Non-comparative sorting: Counting sort and Radix sort.
  - Hash table architectures: Hash functions, collision resolution mechanisms (chaining vs. open addressing: linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing).

CSE202 inculcates enterprise-grade object-oriented software engineering principles using the Java language ecosystem. title: CSE202: Object-Oriented Programming with Java Syllabus and Coding Standards
text:
3. DETAILED THEORY SYLLABUS

3.1 Module 1: Principles of Object-Oriented Design and Java Fundamentals
  - Object-oriented paradigm versus procedural programming: Abstraction, encapsulation, information hiding, modularity.
  - Java virtual machine architecture: Bytecode compilation, JVM memory zones (heap, stack, method area), and automated garbage collection.
  - Classes, constructors, object lifecycle, access specifiers (private, default, protected, public), and immutable class construction.
3.2 Module 2: Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Interfaces
  - Subclassing, method overriding, runtime polymorphism (dynamic method dispatch), and the 'super' keyword.
  - Abstract classes versus interfaces: Default and static interface methods, functional interfaces, and multiple interface inheritance.
3.3 Module 3: Exception Handling and Input/Output Streams
  - Robust application resilience: Checked versus unchecked exceptions, try-catch-finally constructs, multi-catch, and custom domain exceptions.
  - Java I/O streams, byte versus character streams, buffered readers, object serialization, and deserialization security.
3.4 Module 4: Java Collections Framework and Generics
  - Generics: Type parameters, type erasure, bounded type parameters, and wildcard semantics.

2. COURSE DESCRIPTION AND MISSION

CSE301 explores the software layer mediating hardware resources and user applications. The syllabus covers fundamental operating system abstractions: process lifecycle management, preemptive CPU scheduling, inter-process communication, concurrency control, deadlock mitigation, physical and virtual memory architectures, file subsystem organization, and storage virtualization.

title: CSE301: Operating Systems (OS) Syllabus and System Programming Lab
text:
3. THEORY CURRICULUM MODULES

3.1 Module 1: Operating System Structures and Process Abstraction
  - OS objectives, dual-mode operation (user mode vs. kernel mode), privileged instructions, and system call interfaces.
  - Process model: Process Control Block (PCB), process state transitions, context switching mechanics, and process creation via fork() and exec().
3.2 Module 2: CPU Scheduling and Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
  - Scheduling criteria: Throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, and response time.
  - Scheduling algorithms: First-Come First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF), Priority Scheduling, and Round Robin (RR) with dynamic time quantum analysis.
  - Inter-process communication: Shared memory architecture and message passing queues.
3.3 Module 3: Concurrency, Synchronization, and Deadlocks
  - Critical section problem: Race conditions, mutual exclusion, progress, and bounded waiting.
  - Synchronization tools: Peterson's algorithmic solution, hardware atomic instructions (test-and-set), binary and counting semaphores, and mutex locks.
  - Classical synchronization problems: Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and Dining Philosophers.
  - Deadlock characterization: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait. Deadlock prevention, Banker's avoidance algorithm, and detection/recovery.
3.4 Module 4: Memory Management and Virtual Memory
  - Physical memory allocation: Contiguous allocation, fragmentation (internal and external), and dynamic storage partitioning.
  - Paging architectures: Hardware page tables, Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLBs), and multi-level paging.
  - Virtual memory: Demand paging, page fault service routines, and page replacement policies (FIFO, Optimal, LRU, and Second-Chance).
3.5 Module 5: Storage and File Systems
  - Secondary storage hardware, disk scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN), file concept, directory structures, and allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed).

3. CURRICULAR MODULES

3.1 Module 1: Relational Architecture and Conceptual Modeling
  - Limitations of file-based storage, three-schema database architecture (physical, conceptual, external), and data independence.
  - Entity-Relationship (ER) modeling: Entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality ratios, and enhanced ER features (generalization, specialization).
3.2 Module 2: Relational Model and Formal Query Languages
  - Relational model constraints: Domain, key, entity integrity, and referential integrity constraints.
  - Formal query languages: Relational algebra operators (select, project, join, set operations) and tuple relational calculus.
3.3 Module 3: SQL Syntax and Complex Query Processing
  - Data Definition Language (DDL), Data Manipulation Language (DML), and Data Control Language (DCL).
  - Complex SQL queries: Nested subqueries, correlated subqueries, set operations, aggregate functions, and windowing functions.
  - Views, triggers, and stored procedures.
3.4 Module 4: Relational Schema Normalization
  - Anomalies in unnormalized schemas: Insertion, deletion, and modification anomalies.
  - Functional dependencies: Armstrong's axioms, canonical cover, and attribute closure.
  - Normal forms: First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), Third Normal Form (3NF), and Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF). Lossless-join decomposition and dependency preservation.
3.5 Module 5: Transactions, Concurrency, and Recovery
  - Transaction concepts and ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability).
  - Serializability: Conflict and view serializability.
  - Concurrency control techniques: Two-Phase Locking (2PL), timestamp ordering, and deadlock detection.
  - Database recovery architectures: Write-ahead logging (WAL) and checkpointing.

title: MEC204: Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer Laboratory Manual
text:
3. MODULAR THEORY SYLLABUS

3.1 Module 1: Fundamental Thermodynamic Laws and Energy Systems
  - Thermodynamic systems, states, processes, cycles, and pure substances.
  - First Law of Thermodynamics: Conservation of energy in closed and steady-flow open systems.
  - Second Law of Thermodynamics: Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements, Carnot cycle, and entropy generation.
3.2 Module 2: Applied Thermodynamic Cycles
  - Vapor power cycles: Ideal Rankine cycle and reheat/regenerative Rankine modifications.
  - Gas power cycles: Air-standard Otto, Diesel, and dual cycles.
  - Refrigeration cycles: Vapor-compression refrigeration cycle and heat pumps.
3.3 Module 3: Conduction Heat Transfer
  - Fourier's law of heat conduction, thermal conductivity of materials, and general heat conduction equations.
  - One-dimensional steady-state conduction through composite walls, cylinders, and spheres.
  - Extended surfaces (fins): Heat transfer from rectangular and pin fins with various boundary conditions.
3.4 Module 4: Convection Heat Transfer
  - Newton's law of cooling and hydrodynamic/thermal boundary layer fundamentals.
  - Forced convection: Flow over flat plates, flow through circular pipes, and empirical correlations (Nusselt, Reynolds, Prandtl numbers).
  - Free/natural convection over vertical and horizontal plates.

2. PURPOSE AND ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING SCOPE

title: Environmental Engineering Testing Manual: BOD/COD Protocols
text:
3. BIOCHEMICAL OXYGEN DEMAND (BOD) PROTOCOL

3.1 Principle: BOD measures the amount of dissolved molecular oxygen consumed by aerobic microorganisms to biochemically oxidize organic matter present in a wastewater sample during incubation over a specified duration.
3.2 Apparatus and Reagents: 300 mL glass-stoppered BOD incubation bottles, thermostatically controlled BOD incubator (maintained strictly at 20°C +/- 1°C), aerated dilution water, manganous sulfate solution, alkaline-iodide-azide reagent, concentrated sulfuric acid, starch indicator, and standardized sodium thiosulfate (0.025N) titrant.
3.3 Procedure (5-Day 20°C Test):
  - Step 1: Neutralize sample pH (6.5 to 8.5) and prepare appropriate serial dilutions with aerated dilution water.
  - Step 2: Fill two sets of 300 mL BOD bottles to overflowing without entraining air bubbles. Stopper tightly and water-seal the neck.
  - Step 3: Determine Initial Dissolved Oxygen (DO_0) on the first bottle immediately using the Azide Modification of the Winkler Titration Method.
  - Step 4: Incubate the second bottle in the dark inside the BOD incubator at 20°C for exactly 5 days (120 hours).
  - Step 5: On Day 5, withdraw the bottle and determine Final Dissolved Oxygen (DO_5) via Winkler titration.
3.4 Calculation Formula:
  BOD_5 (mg/L) = [(DO_0 - DO_5) - (B_0 - B_5)] * Dilution Factor
  where B_0 and B_5 represent initial and final DO of the blank dilution water.

title: Mechanical Design and Stress Analysis Course Outline
text:
3. THEORY CURRICULUM MODULES

3.1 Module 1: Static Failure Theories and Stress Concentration
  - Multi-axial stress states, principal stresses, and Mohr's circle representation.
  - Static failure criteria: Maximum Normal Stress theory, Maximum Shear Stress theory (Tresca), and Distortion Energy theory (von Mises).
  - Stress concentration factors (K_t) and geometric notch sensitivity.
3.2 Module 2: Fatigue and Dynamic Failure
  - Cyclic loading, S-N curves, endurance limit, and modifying factors (surface finish, size, reliability, temperature).
  - Fluctuating stress analysis: Gerber parabola, Goodman diagram, and Soderberg relation.
3.3 Module 3: Design of Power Transmission Elements
  - Transmission shaft design under combined bending and torsion using ASME design codes.
  - Keyways, splines, rigid and flexible shaft couplings.
3.4 Module 4: Mechanical Fasteners, Welds, and Springs
  - Threaded fasteners, bolt pretension, stiffness matrices, and bolted joint fatigue.
  - Stress analysis of welded joints (butt and fillet welds) under eccentric loads.
  - Design of helical and leaf springs.
3.5 Module 5: Finite Element Analysis (FEA) Principles
  - Discretization, element formulations (1D bar, 2D plane stress, 3D solid elements), boundary constraints, and convergence.

2. CATEGORIZATION OF MALPRACTICE INFRACTIONS

2.1 Level 1 — Minor Procedural Non-Compliance:
  a) Infractions: Possession of unauthorized unwritten paper or blank slips; communicating verbally or via gestures with peers; glancing at another candidate's booklet; refusing to occupy the assigned seat.

  a) Infractions: Possession or utilization of manuscript notes, formula chits, textbook clippings, or scribbled formulas on body parts or apparel; possession or operation of electronic devices (cellular phones, smartwatches, digital earphones, programmable calculators); copying from peer answer books.
  b) Prescribed Penalty: Immediate cancellation of the current paper and comprehensive cancellation of all theory and laboratory examinations registered in the active semester. The candidate is awarded 'F' grades across all registered semester courses and debarred from subsequent papers.
2.3 Level 3 — Gross Institutional Subversion and Collusion:
  a) Infractions: Impersonation of another candidate; smuggling blank or written answer booklets outside the examination hall; tampering with barcoded cover sheets; attempting to bribe or physically threatening invigilation staff; organized electronic leakage.
  b) Prescribed Penalty: Summary cancellation of the entire semester examination result, formal suspension or debarment from Demo University examinations for a period of one to two academic years, eviction from residential hostels, or permanent expulsion from the university.

4.5 Step 5 — Fee Refund Execution: If the final score results in an increase of 10.0% or greater over the original mark, a 50% refund of the re-evaluation fee (Rs. 600) is credited to the student's PayVarsity account.
4.6 Step 6 — Grade Supersession and Publication: The finalized re-evaluation mark permanently replaces the initial grade. Revised electronic grade sheets are published on ExamShield within 15 working days of the application deadline.

2.5 Zero Refund Tier (Beyond 30 Days): Zero percent (0%) refund is admissible if the withdrawal notice is received more than thirty (30) calendar days after the commencement of classes.

section: 3. TROUBLESHOOTING PAYMENT FAILURES AND BANKING GLITCHES (CHAL-06)
subsection: 3.1 Scenario A — Account Debited but Status 'Pending' on Portal
text:
3. TROUBLESHOOTING PAYMENT FAILURES AND BANKING GLITCHES (CHAL-06)

3.1 Scenario A — Account Debited but Status 'Pending' on Portal:
- Root Cause: Intermittent communication timeout between the external banking aggregator and the university gateway during peak registration traffic.
- Standard Resolution: The automated reconciliation daemon executes batch queries every two (2) hours. In ninety-five percent of cases, payment status updates automatically to 'Settled' within four (4) hours.
- Helpdesk Escalation: If status remains pending after twenty-four (24) hours, the student must log a ResolveDesk ticket under 'Finance > Payment Reconciliation', attaching bank transaction statement showing the unique 12-digit UTR number.
3.2 Scenario B — Dual Deduction / Duplicate Payment:
- Root Cause: Multiple payment attempts triggered when the initial gateway session lagged.
- Automated Rectification: Duplicate debits identified during nightly banking audits are automatically flagged for reverse settlement. Excess funds are credited back to the originating bank account within five to seven (5–7) working days.
3.3 Scenario C — E-Challan Offline Payment Delay:
- NEFT/RTGS payments processed via bank branches require up to twenty-four (24) business hours for inter-bank clearance and manual UTR reconciliation in the finance accounts ledger.

title: University Procurement, Tendering, and Purchase Order Protocol
text:
3. REQUISITION AND PROCUREMENT WORKFLOW

All institutional procurement must adhere to a multi-tier authorization workflow executed on UniCampus ERP:
3.1 Tier 1 — Requisition Indent: The department Lab In-Charge or Research Principal Investigator drafts an electronic Purchase Requisition (PR) detailing technical specifications, quantity, estimated cost, and designated budget head (Department CAPEX or Sponsored Research Grant).
3.2 Tier 2 — Departmental Scrutiny & Endorsement: The academic Head of Department (HOD) verifies curriculum or research necessity and signs off on the indent.
3.3 Tier 3 — Quotation Audit & Comparative Tendering:
- Minor Purchases (< Rs. 50,000): Sourced directly through approved institutional rate contracts.
- Moderate Purchases (Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000): Requires minimum three (3) competitive written quotations scrutinized by the Department Purchase Committee.
- Major Capital Purchases (> Rs. 5,00,000): Requires formal open tender publishing and evaluation by the Central Purchase and Tendering Board.
3.4 Tier 4 — Financial Vetting & PO Generation: The Finance and Accounts Office audits vendor quotes, verifies tax compliance (GSTIN), validates budget availability, and generates the numbered Purchase Order (PO) signed by the Chief Finance Officer and Registrar.

4. ANTI-PLAGIARISM VERIFICATION AND THRESHOLDS (RES-ETH-001)

Prior to repository archiving, all dissertations and theses must undergo rigorous computerized similarity analysis administered by the Plagiarism & Thesis Verification Unit:
4.1 Authorized Verification Engines: Similarity evaluation is performed exclusively using university-licensed Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub platforms.

title: Central Library Services, Off-Campus E-Access, and Book Bank FAQs
text:
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS: CENTRAL LIBRARY AND LEARNING RESOURCE CENTRE

Q1: What are the standard operating hours of the Central Library?
A: General Circulation Stacks, Book Issue Desks, and the Reference Hall operate from 08:00 AM to 10:00 PM on all official working days, and from 09:00 AM to 05:00 PM on Saturdays, Sundays, and notified university holidays. The Ground Floor 24/7 Reading Room remains open round-the-clock, 365 days a year, accessible via RFID card turnstiles (CampusPass).

Q2: What is the borrowing quota and loan duration for undergraduate and postgraduate students?
A: Under POL-LIBRARY:
- Undergraduate (UG) Students: May borrow up to 4 books for 14 calendar days;
- Postgraduate (PG) Students / Research Scholars: May borrow up to 6 books for 28 calendar days;
- Faculty Members: May borrow up to 10 books for 90 days (semester loan).

Q3: What are the overdue fine rates if I return a book late?
A: Overdue fines are calculated automatically by LibNet at Rs. 5 per day per book for the first 7 days of delay, increasing to Rs. 10 per day per book from Day 8 onwards. If your unpaid fine balance exceeds Rs. 50, your library account is automatically locked, preventing further checkouts or renewals.

Q4: What is the Book Bank Scheme and who is eligible to apply?
A: The Book Bank is a specialized social and academic welfare service operated by the Central Library. It provides a complete set of required core engineering and management textbooks for the entire semester to eligible students:
- Category A: Students belonging to SC/ST communities upon verification of category documentation;
- Category B: Economically Weaker Section (EWS) students with verified family annual income below Rs. 2,50,000.
Book Bank sets are issued during the first two weeks of every semester and must be returned within seven (7) days following the completion of Semester End Examinations (SEE).

Q5: Why is my Semester End Exam hall ticket or course registration blocked due to library dues?
A: Under institutional workflow REL-006 and POL-LIBRARY, complete clearance of all library obligations (zero outstanding overdue fines and complete return of circulating volumes) is mandatory. Uncleared fines or unreturned books trigger an automated financial/administrative hold flag in UniCampus ERP, blocking exam hall ticket downloads on ExamShield and preventing online course registration.

Q6: How do I access IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and ACM Digital Library from off-campus?
A: Authenticate through the LibNet Off-Campus E-Journal Proxy Gateway at https://libnet.demo.edu.internal/opac using your standard UniCampus ERP Single Sign-On credentials. Automated crawling or sharing credentials with external parties is strictly prohibited under IT-POL-001.

Students who lose or damage their RFID credential must execute the following five-step restoration protocol:
4.1 Step 1 (Immediate Security Deactivation): The student logs into ResolveDesk (SYS-RESOLVE) and logs an urgent ticket under 'Security > Lost ID Card'. The CampusPass engine immediately blacklists the lost RFID chip serial number to prevent unauthorized facility ingress.
4.2 Step 2 (Fee Settlement): The student pays the non-refundable duplicate card issuance fee of Rs. 500 online via PayVarsity (SYS-PAY) under the incidental fees schedule (FIN-POL-002) and saves the generated digital receipt.
4.3 Step 3 (Identity Verification): The student presents the PayVarsity fee receipt along with a recognized government photo ID (Aadhaar, Passport, or Voter ID) at the Central Security Office (Main Entrance Gate).
4.4 Step 4 (Card Printing and Encoding): Security personnel verify active enrollment in UniCampus ERP and print a new smart card encoded with a refreshed RFID chip serial number.
4.5 Step 5 (System Synchronization and SLA): The new credential is issued within forty-eight (48) hours of fee payment. CampusPass automatically synchronizes the new RFID chip identifier with the LibNet library database, DormTrack hostel turnstiles, and TransPass commuter portals.

title: Campus Emergency Evacuation and Fire Disaster Management Protocol
text:
2. IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY DISCOVERY AND REPORTING

2.1 Raising the Alarm: Any individual discovering a fire, smoke plume, or life-threatening hazard must immediately break the glass of the nearest Manual Call Point (MCP) fire alarm pull station located along corridor corridors and stairwell exits.
2.2 Emergency Notification: Immediately contact the 24/7 Security Operations Centre Hotline (Extension 100 / Direct Campus Emergency Line: +91-80-2345-0100). State clearly:
- Exact building name, floor number, and room/laboratory identifier;
- Nature of the hazard (Electrical fire, Chemical spill, Structural failure);
- Known human casualties or trapped personnel.
2.3 Automated Alarm Transmission: Fire panel activation automatically triggers localized audible sirens, unlatches electromagnetic emergency exit doors, and notifies municipal fire dispatch.

5. INCIDENT COMMAND, HEADCOUNTS, AND MEDICAL TRIAGE

5.1 Accountability Verification: Department Floor Wardens conduct rapid headcount reconciliations against active attendance rosters and report missing personnel to the Incident Commander (CSO) within ten (10) minutes of arrival.
5.2 Emergency Medical Response: The Senior Chief Medical Officer (ROLE-CMO) coordinates emergency ambulance dispatch from the Campus Health Centre, establishing an on-site first-aid triage tent at the perimeter of the assembly area.
5.3 All-Clear Authorization: Re-entry into evacuated buildings is strictly forbidden until the Chief Security Officer and Municipal Fire Chief formally declare an 'All-Clear' over the public address system.
5.4 Mandatory Drills: Full-scale fire evacuation and disaster response drills are conducted semi-annually across all academic blocks and student residences.

text:
3. INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION AND SEVERITY TIERS

Reported security incidents are categorized into three operational tiers:
3.1 Tier 1 (Minor Operational Incidents): Misplaced personal items, unattended bicycle theft at external gates, minor parking scrapes, or perimeter noise complaints. Handled directly by Gate Security Duty Officers within twenty-four (24) hours.
3.2 Tier 2 (Moderate Security Infractions): Forced room entry, theft of computing hardware or lab components, deliberate damage to estate fixtures, or unauthorized visitor access after hours. Preliminary enquiry completed within forty-eight (48) hours; investigative dossier forwarded to the Proctorial Board (STU-POL-005).
3.3 Tier 3 (Critical / Major Offenses): Physical assault, possession or distribution of narcotics/alcohol, ragging incidents (STU-POL-004), weapon possession, or major estate sabotage. Demands instant physical restraint, interim campus suspension, and formal transmission of an FIR to local municipal police with Vice-Chancellor ratification.

2.4 Extended Library Shuttle: A specialized night transit shuttle departs at 07:00 PM on working days to accommodate students and research scholars utilizing the Central Library and computing laboratories.

text:
1. PURPOSE AND STATUTORY GOVERNANCE

These regulations govern the admission, enrollment, supervisory assignment, curriculum credit requirements, progress milestones, comprehensive examination, and thesis evaluation procedures for candidates registered for the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree at Demo University.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
retrieval_signals: full time to part time PhD conversion

title: Regulations Governing Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Degrees
text:
2. ENROLLMENT MODES AND DEGREE DURATION

2.1 Enrollment Categories: Candidates are admitted under Full-Time (FT) scholar status (supported by institutional fellowships or external sponsored project grants) or Part-Time status (for working professionals and in-service faculty).
- Entity Disambiguation: Full-Time (FT) doctoral enrollment must not be confused with student Field Trips (FT under ACAD-SOP-008).
2.2 Program Duration: The standard minimum doctoral duration is four (4) academic years (8 semesters). In accordance with university academic regulations, the maximum allowable period for thesis submission is N + 2 years (a total ceiling of six years from initial registration).
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
retrieval_signals: full time to part time PhD conversion

title: Regulations Governing Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Degrees
text:
3. DOCTORAL COURSEWORK AND ACADEMIC BENCHMARKS (PROG-PHD-ENG)

3.1 Mandatory Credit Load: Every registered research scholar must earn a minimum of fourteen (14) graduate-level coursework credits:
- RES801: Research Methodology and Quantitative Analysis (Core, 4 Credits)
- RES802: Research and Publication Ethics (Core, 2 Credits)
- Departmental Advanced Technical Electives (8 Credits)
3.2 Minimum Grade Standard: Scholars must attain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 7.00 across completed coursework subjects before they are permitted to attempt the comprehensive examination.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
retrieval_signals: full time to part time PhD conversion

title: Regulations Governing Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Degrees
text:
4. DOCTORAL COMMITTEE (DC) AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT

4.1 Committee Constitution: Within sixty (60) days of enrollment, the Dean of Research constitutes a dedicated Doctoral Committee (DC) comprising the Research Supervisor (Convener), Head of Department or nominee, two senior internal faculty experts, and one approved external subject specialist.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Doctoral Committee (DC) under DEPT-RES must not be confused with the Disciplinary Committee (DC under DEPT-SW / STU-POL-005) or the Direct Current Hardware Laboratory (DC under DEPT-ECE / ECE-LAB-002).
4.2 Comprehensive Examination: Upon finishing prescribed coursework, the scholar must pass a written and oral comprehensive examination administered by the DC to assess foundational mastery in the research domain.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
retrieval_signals: full time to part time PhD conversion

title: Regulations Governing Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Degrees
text:
5. THESIS SUBMISSION AND DEFENSE

Following successful completion of semi-annual progress reviews (RES-POL-002), mandatory publication requirements, and certified plagiarism verification under RES-ETH-001, the scholar presents a public pre-synopsis colloquium. Upon DC endorsement, the final Ph.D. thesis is dispatched to two independent external evaluators for blind adjudication, culminating in an open oral defense viva voce.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation

title: Doctoral Committee Progress Report (PR) Submission Guidelines

3.1 Review Windows: Formal doctoral progress reviews are executed twice per academic calendar year:
- Odd Semester Cycle: Scheduled during June–July.
- Even Semester Cycle: Scheduled during December–January.
3.2 Submission Workflow on ResTrack:
- Step 1: The research scholar compiles the standardized PR dossier detailing literature surveys, experimental results, simulation data, chapter drafts, and publication manuscripts.

title: Research Ethics, Academic Integrity, and Plagiarism Prevention Code
text:
1. PURPOSE AND ETHICAL MANDATE

This institutional code establishes the binding ethical standards, integrity expectations, plagiarism detection limits, and review board clearance workflows governing all scientific inquiry, doctoral dissertations, postgraduate theses, and scholarly publications produced at Demo University.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
roles: Chairperson of Research Ethics Review Board

title: Research Ethics, Academic Integrity, and Plagiarism Prevention Code
section: 2. PLAGIARISM TOLERANCE THRESHOLDS AND THESIS CLEARANCE
text:
2. PLAGIARISM TOLERANCE THRESHOLDS AND THESIS CLEARANCE

2.1 Statutory Ten Percent (10%) Threshold: In accordance with university academic regulations and national research integrity norms, the maximum permissible textual similarity index for all Ph.D. theses and M.Tech dissertations is strictly ten percent (<= 10%), excluding bibliography, mathematical equations, and standard institutional affiliations.
2.2 Mandatory Verification Protocol: All thesis manuscripts must be submitted to the Plagiarism & Thesis Verification Unit at the Valmiki Central Library for formal scanning using Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub prior to final submission (LIB-POL-004). An official, digitally signed Similarity Clearance Certificate must accompany every submitted thesis.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
roles: Chairperson of Research Ethics Review Board

title: Research Ethics, Academic Integrity, and Plagiarism Prevention Code
text:
3. RESEARCH ETHICS REVIEW BOARD (RERB) CLEARANCE

3.1 Mandatory Ethical Approval: Experimental research involving human participants, private personal data, biometric surveillance, or animal specimens requires formal advance clearance from the Research Ethics Review Board (RERB).
3.2 Protocol Submission: Researchers must upload experimental consent forms, participant privacy safeguards, and risk-mitigation plans on ResTrack Portal prior to commencing clinical or field investigations.
department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
roles: Chairperson of Research Ethics Review Board

title: Research Ethics, Academic Integrity, and Plagiarism Prevention Code
text:
4. SCHOLARLY INTEGRITY BREACHES AND SANCTIONS

Fabrication of experimental results, data falsification, duplicate publication, ghost authorship, or intentional plagiarism exceeding statutory limits constitutes severe scientific malpractice. Verified infractions result in immediate thesis rejection, revocation of research fellowships, cancellation of doctoral registration, and formal disciplinary proceedings before the Proctorial Board.

title: Student Grievance Redressal and Ombudsman Policy
text:
2. SCOPE AND JURISDICTION

2.1 Cognizable Grievances: A formal grievance may be lodged regarding:
  a) Academic Irregularities: Arbitrary or discriminatory internal grading, denial of sanctioned On-Duty leave, or unnotified syllabus deviations.
  b) Administrative Deficiencies: Inordinate delays in publishing results, issuing bonafide letters, or processing fee adjustments and refunds.
  c) Campus Facilities & Services: Persistent failure in hostel maintenance, mess hygiene, transportation routes, or digital library access.
  d) Victimization and Harassment: Discrimination based on gender, caste, creed, regional origin, or physical disability.
2.2 Excluded Matters: Disciplinary sanctions imposed by the Proctorial Board and sexual harassment complaints (governed exclusively by the Internal Complaints Committee) fall outside the purview of this policy.

title: Campus Health Centre Medical Verification and Outpatient Consultation SOP
text:
3. MEDICAL DOCUMENTATION VERIFICATION WORKFLOW (PROC-MED-COND / REL-004)

When a student is absent due to acute illness or hospitalization and seeks academic attendance condonation, the following sequential workflow is mandatory:
3.1 Step 1 — In-Person Presentation: Within 3 working days of resuming academic attendance, the student must visit the Medical Verification Desk carrying complete original hospital records: clinical case history, discharge summary, registered doctor prescriptions, and laboratory investigation receipts.
3.2 Step 2 — Physician Audit: The Senior Chief Medical Officer examines the patient, scrutinizes diagnostic dates against class absence dates, cross-verifies hospital registration numbers, and validates clinical authenticity.
3.3 Step 3 — Verification Slip Issuance: Upon authenticating the illness, the Medical Officer generates an official University Medical Verification Slip in HealthDesk featuring a unique digital verification code and medical stamp.
3.4 Step 4 — ResolveDesk Upload: The student uploads a scanned copy of the endorsed medical slip to ResolveDesk under 'Medical Leave Submission' to notify their Faculty Advisor and HOD.
3.5 Step 5 — Academic Transmission: The department endorses the verified medical slip and routes it to the Dean of Academic Affairs to adjust attendance calculations within the 65.0% to 74.9% condonation band.
